# The computing environment {#sec-computing}

Sequencing files are too large for a laptop, so the processing happens on
**Longleaf**, UNC's computing cluster. This chapter covers the minimum you need:
logging in, moving around, looking at files, and asking the cluster to run a job.

## What a cluster is

A cluster is many computers (**nodes**) that share one file system. You log
in to a **login node**, which is shared by everyone and meant only for
light work: editing files, copying, submitting jobs. The real work runs on
**compute nodes**, which you request through a scheduler called **SLURM**.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  L["Your laptop"] -- ssh --> LN["Login node<br/>(light work only)"]
  LN -- "sbatch / srun" --> S["SLURM scheduler"]
  S --> C1["Compute node"]
  S --> C2["Compute node"]
  S --> C3["Compute node"]
  C1 & C2 & C3 --- FS[("Shared storage<br/>/proj, /work, /users")]
  LN --- FS
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Don't run FastQC, Salmon, HISAT2 or anything else heavy directly on the login node.
It slows the node down for everyone and the job may be killed. Use an
interactive job (below) or `sbatch`.
:::

## Logging in

From the Terminal app on a Mac (or PowerShell on Windows):

```bash
ssh your_onyen@longleaf.unc.edu
```

## Where things live

| Location | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `/nas/longleaf/home/<onyen>` (`~`) | Your home folder; small, backed up. Scripts and configs |
| `/work/users/j/d/jdoe` (first letter, second letter, onyen) | Large, fast scratch space for running pipelines. **Not backed up, and old files are purged** |
| `/proj/phanstiel_lab/` | Lab project space: raw data, references, shared results |

A sensible habit: keep raw FASTQs in `/proj`, run pipelines in `/work`, and copy
the results you want to keep back to `/proj`.

## Ten commands to start with

```bash
pwd                      # print working directory: where am I?
ls -lh                   # list files, with human-readable sizes
cd /proj/phanstiel_lab   # change directory
cd ..                    # go up one level
mkdir -p myproject/raw   # make a folder (and parents)
cp file.txt backup/      # copy
mv old.txt new.txt       # move or rename
less file.txt            # page through a file (q to quit)
zcat reads.fastq.gz | head -8   # first 8 lines of a gzipped file
wc -l file.txt           # count lines
```

Press **Tab** to autocomplete file names. It saves typing and prevents typos.

## Software: modules

Longleaf has many versions of each tool installed, and you pick one with
`module`. This is exactly what bagPipes does at the top of each rule:

```bash
module avail salmon          # what versions exist?
module load salmon/1.10.3    # use this one
salmon --version
module list                  # what do I have loaded?
module purge                 # unload everything
```

## Running jobs with SLURM

### Interactive jobs: for trying things out

```bash
srun -p interact -n 1 --mem=8g -t 2:00:00 --pty bash
```

This gives you a shell on a compute node for two hours. Everything in the
hands-on parts of this book can be run inside one of these.

### Batch jobs: for real runs

You write a script with `#SBATCH` lines describing what you need, and
submit it. `RNApipe.sh` in bagPipes is one of these:

```bash
#! /bin/bash -login
#SBATCH -J RNApipeCore      # job name
#SBATCH -t 4320             # time limit in minutes (3 days)
#SBATCH -p general          # partition (queue)
#SBATCH --mem=2gb           # memory
#SBATCH -o "%x-%j.out"      # log file: <jobname>-<jobid>.out
```

```bash
sbatch RNApipe.sh            # submit
squeue -u $USER              # what's running / waiting?
sacct -j 123456 --format=JobID,JobName,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS   # how did it go?
scancel 123456               # cancel a job
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Why does `RNApipe.sh` only ask for 2 GB?

That job only runs **Snakemake**, which acts as a manager. Snakemake then
submits each step (FastQC, Salmon, ...) as its own SLURM job with its own
memory request. You'll see dozens of jobs appear in `squeue`. See
[Snakemake in plain language](snakemake.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding

1. You want to look at the first read in a FASTQ file. Is it OK to do that
   on the login node?
2. Where should a 200 GB pipeline output folder go while it is being made?
3. What does `module load trim_galore/0.6.10` do?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Answers

1. Yes. `zcat file.fastq.gz | head -4` is light work.
2. `/work`, which is fast and large. Copy the results you want to keep to `/proj`
   afterwards, because `/work` is purged.
3. It puts that version of Trim Galore (and its dependency, Cutadapt) on your
   `PATH` so the `trim_galore` command works in this shell.
:::
:::
